name: U201 anode sense
question: How should U201 pin 2 (the LM74910's anode sense) be joined to VBAT_IN?
why_now: The board is routed under D33 B with one functional join left open: U201 pin 2 needs VBAT_IN, and no layer the rules allow gets it there without re-laying lines routed today. C510 pad 1 and test points TP301 and TP401 are also open; those need work, not a decision.

facts.label: Where pin 2 is
facts.value: On U201's west side, in the notch of the VBAT_D pour under the GND busbar, 14.7 mm east of the west VBAT_IN pour (Q201's source pads) and 22 mm west of the east one.
facts.source: node60.kicad_pcb: U201 pin 2 at (151.1, 76.25); PWR_VBAT_IN_W to x 136.4

facts.label: Why F.Cu is closed to it
facts.value: VBAT_IN is class PWR_BATT. D33 B allows signal tracks on F.Cu under the GND bar but no battery-net track: the line sits at battery potential ahead of every protection, and only the harness fuse would clear a short to the bar.
facts.source: node60.kicad_dru, rule 'F.Cu under the GND busbar: no battery-net tracks'

facts.label: Why B.Cu is closed to it today
facts.value: West of the pin: LM_SW's via, R204's pads, C211, then the six lane lines of the west channel running east on B.Cu at y 69.3 to 71.2. In2 may carry tracks only north of y 70, which is north of those lines.

facts.label: State before this run
facts.value: Open on main since the placement landed: the fast routes never closed it and the hand route was left to you.
facts.source: commit b404f9c DRC: 'Zone PWR_VBAT_IN_W | Pad 2 of U201'

options.name: Re-lay the lines in its way
options.summary: No rule changes. LM_SW, LM_UVLO and the R204 to R205 link move to F.Cu with vias in their pads (they are resistor-limited, so D33 B allows them); the west channel's lines are routed again north of the band so that VBAT_IN can run on B.Cu out of the notch, hop over them on In2 north of y 70, and drop into the west VBAT_IN pour beside Q201.

images.caption: Pin 2 is the dark blue pin on U201's west side; the west VBAT_IN pour is the blue area at the left. The six grey lines turning north-east above the pour are the west channel's lines.

measures.label: Lines routed today that are routed again

gains: The battery-net rule you chose today stays whole
The sense line never leaves B.Cu and In2
costs: An hour or more of routing and checking; the six west lines and their test points move again
The sense line is longer than a direct one and passes close to SPI lines on In2

options.name: One exception: this line on F.Cu under the GND bar
options.summary: Add U201's sense track to the GND-busbar rule as a named exception: one 0.15 mm VBAT_IN track on F.Cu, about 15 mm, from a via beside pin 2 west to Q201's source pads, under solder mask like the signal tracks.
gains: Short and direct, the way the LM74910 wants its anode sense
costs: A track at battery potential, with nothing but its own 0.15 mm width to limit a fault, 0.6 mm under the grounded bar
An exception to a rule made the same day

options.name: Leave it for hand routing
options.summary: The board stays as it is on main; you route pin 2 in KiCad. `unconnected_items` stays a warning until then.
gains: Nothing moves until you have looked at the routed board
costs: The ideal-diode controller has no anode connection until it is done: the board is not ready for a `rev-*` tag

recommendation.why: **A.** It keeps the rule as you set it, and everything it moves is copper routed today. B is quicker and electrically neater, but it puts the one kind of track the rule exists to keep out under the bar.

answer: Reply with A, B or C, or a change to one.
